papers.title: Aggregation Rules Induced by KL-Regularised Preference Dynamics on Networks
papers.abstract: We study agents that each align a model to their own preference data while observing one another, and ask which aggregation rule the resulting policies implement. Each round, an agent takes one KL-regularised step. The step involves a reference that the agent is penalised for leaving and a challenger against which its responses are compared, and each of the two may be the agent's own or an average over the agents it observes; attention need not be reciprocal. Aggregating the reference makes the rule collective. Agent $v$ then has the weight $\pi_v/\beta_v$, its share of the network's long-run attention divided by its temperature. If, in addition, the challenger is fixed, the agents concentrate on the response maximising $\sum_v(\pi_v/\beta_v)r_v(y)$, where $r_v$ is agent $v$'s reward, and the rule is cardinal. If the reference is fixed and the challenger aggregated, the agents' policies at a fixed point generally differ, and any weighted mean of them is an approximate maximal lottery whatever the weights, so the dynamics select no weighting. If both are aggregated, the rule is ordinal: averaged over rounds, the collective policy is a maximal lottery of the influence-weighted preference kernel, up to a slack that we bound. Where a collective rule exists, its weights depend only on the attention weights and the temperatures.

papers.title: One-shot identification of analytic systems
papers.abstract: We study when the coefficients of a linearly parameterized analytic system can be identified from a single input-solution pair. Given a finite dictionary of analytic operators, each admissible input induces a finite-dimensional linear recovery map from coefficients to observed outputs. Coefficient recovery is possible exactly when this map is injective. We define the degenerate input set as the set of inputs for which injectivity fails and prove a zero-one law: either every admissible input is degenerate, or the degenerate set is negligible in the sense that it is compactly slice-null and has zero measure under every nondegenerate Gaussian measure. We then apply this framework to the recovery of matrices, analytic continuous-time dynamical systems, and differential operators. For several ODE and PDE classes, we further characterize the degenerate sets explicitly and identify deterministic choices of inputs that guarantee recovery.

papers.title: On rescuing diverging algorithms: crossing infinity in continuous Newton methods via a self-similarity detection framework
papers.abstract: We address the solution of systems of nonlinear algebraic equations via continuous Newton methods; these methods reformulate the discrete Newton update as an initial value problem for a system of ordinary differential equations (ODEs) whose stationary points correspond to the desired roots. A fundamental challenge arises when the Jacobian of these ODEs becomes singular along the solution trajectory, inducing blow-up in the vector field --or in the state itself-- and causing the numerical integration to break down before reaching the desired root. To overcome this difficulty, we propose a directional self-similar blow-up detection and crossing procedure, wrapped around an adaptive step-size ODE solver with event detection. The method assumes local self-similar behavior near the blow-up; the self-similarity exponent, blow-up time, and amplitude are estimated on the fly from a short sequence of threshold crossings via linear regression, requiring no prior knowledge of the singularity location, its order, or the blow-up regime---in contrast to approaches that rely on explicit analytical continuation or problem-specific coordinate transformations. The estimated exponent distinguishes two qualitatively different scenarios at finite time: one in which only the vector field diverges while the state remains finite, admitting an explicit integral correction, and one in which the state itself blows-up. In addition, infinite-time divergence of the state (the so-called "grow-up" regime) is handled through a suitable time reparameterization. In higher dimensions, we track the norm of the vector field along its instantaneous direction; near a simple singularity, the flow asymptotically aligns with a single dominant direction (see text), reducing detection and estimation to a scalar problem regardless of ambient space dimension.

papers.title: Rollout Scheduling for Chaotic Neural ODEs: Coverage Gains, Computational Cost, and Predictive Accuracy
papers.abstract: Training Neural Ordinary Differential Equations (Neural ODEs) on chaotic systems is difficult because small changes in model parameters can lead to rapidly growing differences in predictions. A rollout is a trajectory predicted by the model. Choosing its length from a single global Lyapunov time overlooks differences in local instability. We study rollout scheduling for training on one contiguous rollout per sampled state, asking whether adapting its length to local instability improves prediction. We find the schedule that uses the most trajectory data under an instability budget, a limit on how much instability any one rollout may accumulate. Under stated assumptions, we bound the resulting coverage gain and the coverage lost when the instability estimates are in error. Numerical checks illustrate the theory. Training experiments on Lorenz-63, Lorenz-96, and Kuramoto--Sivashinsky compare adaptive and constant schedules at the same instability budgets and maximum rollout lengths. The budgets are computed from the true system's finite-time Lyapunov exponents. Across the tested settings, adaptive schedules increase trajectory coverage at additional computational cost, without showing a consistent improvement in prediction accuracy. On Lorenz-63, limiting adaptive rollouts to the horizon used to estimate instability improves prediction at the larger budgets. On Kuramoto--Sivashinsky, most configurations provide useful short-time predictions, while all tested long rollouts eventually fail. These findings show why coverage, prediction accuracy, and long-time behavior need separate evaluation, and why instability estimates should be checked over the windows used in training.

papers.title: Embedding Capabilities of Neural ODEs
papers.abstract: Neural ordinary differential equations (neural ODEs) are a class of neural networks that have gained particular interest in recent years. We study input-output relations of neural ODEs using dynamical systems theory and prove several results about the exact embedding of maps in different neural ODE architectures in low and high dimensions. The embedding capability of a neural ODE architecture can be increased by adding, for example, affine linear layers or augmenting the phase space. However, there is currently no systematic theory available, and our work contributes towards this goal by developing various embedding results as well as identifying situations where no embedding is possible. Our core mathematical techniques include iterative functional equations, Morse functions, and suspension flows, as well as several further ideas from analysis. Although in practice mostly universal approximation theorems are used, our geometric dynamical systems viewpoint on universal embedding provides a fundamental understanding of why certain neural ODE architectures perform better than others.

papers.title: Deep Learning of Solver-Aware Turbulence Closures from Nudged LES Dynamics
papers.abstract: The differentiable physics paradigm may be leveraged as an a-posteriori approach for discovering turbulence closure models by embedding a neural network parameterization directly inside the solver and optimizing it given potentially sparse target data. This addresses a key limitation of a-priori learning where direct numerical simulation (DNS) data is used to approximate the subgrid stress with the assumption of a low-pass filter. Closures trained in this a-priori manner frequently lead to unstable deployments due to the mismatch between the assumed filter and the effect of numerical discretizations and coarse-graining. In comparison, while typically stable during deployment, a-posteriori learning incurs high computational costs due to the need to backpropagate through a large eddy simulation (LES) solver. Furthermore, a-posteriori methods are challenging to apply broadly since they require significant modification of existing solvers. Finally, both approaches are limited when generalization is desired across different numerical schemes with their implicit filtering characteristics. In this work, we present a deep-learning approach for turbulence closure modeling built on the continuous data assimilation framework. Our approach enables the a-priori training of closures using DNS data observed only at coarse-grid points without modifying or differentiating through the LES solver, while preserving stability during deployment for the recovery of long-term statistics. We focus on the model's ability to adapt to different discretizations by explicitly conditioning it on the numerical scheme. We use two- and three-dimensional canonical cases to test our framework and show that the learned correction systematically tracks the discretization error of the coarse solver.

papers.title: Characterization of stability radii for robustly asymptotically stable dissipative Hamiltonian differential-algebraic systems
papers.abstract: We study linear time-invariant dissipative Hamiltonian differential-algebraic systems. We characterize when the systems are robustly asymptotically stable and derive exact conditions and bounds when this property is lost under structure-preserving perturbations.

papers.title: Nonlinear Moments as Equivalence Classes: A Lyapunov-Perron Approach to the Invariance Equation
authors: Heein Park (Automation Systems and Research Institute
Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering
Hyeonyeong Jang (Automation Systems and Research Institute
Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering
Electrical and Mathematical Sciences and Engineering Division
King Abdullah University of Science and Technology
Hyungbo Shim (Automation Systems and Research Institute
Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering
Jin Gyu Lee (Automation Systems and Research Institute
Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering
papers.abstract: The linear moment is well defined whenever the system and the exosystem have disjoint spectra. Its nonlinear counterpart is not: the existence and uniqueness of solutions to the invariance equation that defines it are in general not guaranteed, so additional assumptions such as Poisson stability of the exosystem and the exponential stability of the system are required to define the nonlinear moment. This paper reduces this asymmetry. By using the Lyapunov--Perron fixed-point argument, we show that under a condition called the strip condition, there exist local $\mathcal C^N$ solutions, with $N$ determined by the system and the exosystem, and every pair of $\mathcal C^1$ solutions has contact of order $k^-$, where $k$ is a spectral ratio determined by the system and the exosystem; the solutions are flat-equivalent when $k=\infty$. Based on this observation, we extend the concept of nonlinear moment as an equivalence class of functions rather than a function. The polynomial of degree $N$ or formal power series ansatz of the invariance equation are the distinguished representatives of the equivalence class. We also show that, when the system is exponentially stable, the moment describes the output shared by all trajectories up to the order $k^-$, which gives the moment a time-domain interpretation when the steady-state interpretation is not available. Finally, we show that the concept of moment matching also naturally extends as the definition of nonlinear moment is extended to an equivalence class. The ansatz also plays a crucial role in the extended notion of moment matching. The results are illustrated by a numerical example.

papers.title: Principal Eigenvalues for Transport-Nonlocal Operators on Compact Manifolds: Ergodic Averages and Quotient Reduction
papers.abstract: We study principal eigenvalues for transport--nonlocal operators on connected compact Riemannian manifolds. Transport changes the natural spectral threshold from the pointwise maximum of the potential to a maximal invariant average. We establish a necessary and sufficient criterion based on a resolvent spectral radius and derive sufficient existence conditions for uniquely ergodic flows and, through quotient reduction, for flows arising from compact abelian Lie group actions. Examples on the two-dimensional torus show that, for weak nonlocal coupling, transport can create or suppress principal eigenvalues, while sphere rotations illustrate how the quotient criterion accommodates singular orbits.

papers.title: A uniform Picard-rank bound for Calabi Yau threefolds with finitely many flop chambers
papers.abstract: We prove that a smooth projective strict Calabi Yau threefold of sufficiently large Picard number either has infinitely many marked flop chambers or admits a fibration on a smooth flop model.

papers.title: A Keller--Segel Chemotaxis Model on One-Dimensional Moving Domains
papers.abstract: We study a one-dimensional Keller--Segel system on an interval whose boundary moves according to a prescribed contracting law. The boundary motion makes the problem genuinely nonautonomous and destroys the mass conservation available on fixed domains. A time-dependent change of variables, combined with a time reparametrization, reduces the problem to a semilinear system on a fixed interval with time-independent principal part and nonautonomous transport terms. We prove global well-posedness and regularity of weak solutions, and we show that the contraction of the domain yields a uniform bound on the total mass. For the long-time dynamics, our main tool is a singular Gronwall type inequality with an exponentially damped kernel, for which we provide a self-contained version with explicit decay rate and constants, tailored to our setting; under a small gain condition on the boundary velocities, it yields dissipativity with an explicit exponential decay rate, which cannot be obtained from the classical inequality of Henry. With it we prove the existence of the minimal pullback attractor in the universe of families of bounded sets, on the moving domain and then on the fixed rescaled reference domains. Finally, numerical simulations on contracting domains illustrate the effect of the boundary motion on cell aggregation.

papers.title: Holomorphic Foliations with a Single Singularity on Orbifold Projective Surfaces
papers.abstract: We investigate holomorphic foliations on orbifold projective surfaces with cyclic divisor class group, assuming that the foliation has a unique singular point of algebraic multiplicity one. If the normal degree of the foliation is sufficiently large, then we prove that it admits no invariant algebraic curve. Furthermore, we present several examples showing that the bound obtained is optimal.

papers.title: Analytical solution of general interface problems for reaction-advection-diffusion equations
papers.abstract: We obtain novel integral representations, expressed as contour integrals in the complex Fourier plane, for the solution of fully nonhomogeneous interface problems for classical reaction-advection-diffusion (RAD) equations with arbitrary initial data on the line and general interface conditions at the origin. Such problems of applied mathematics emerge in a spectacular variety of physical phenomena in mathematical physics, chemistry, continuum mechanics, biology, pharmacokinetics, as well as mathematical finance. A suitable implementation of Fokas' unified transform method is in force herein, with particular challenges arising due to inclusion in the model of lower-order terms, and the generality of interface problems under consideration. To our knowledge, this careful analysis has not appeared in (nor does it follow easily from) literature published so far. Our explicit formulae directly lend themselves to explorations of solutions' qualitative properties such as regularity, asymptotic behavior and well-posedness. This work has also been of utility in the investigation of nonlinear counterparts as well as in the study of phase-transition phenomena, moving-interface and diffuse-interface problems. Such results for RAD and high-order PDEs will soon appear in a series of separate papers.

papers.title: Analytical modelling of compliance dynamics under fiscal feedback: tipping thresholds, intervention costs and hysteresis
papers.abstract: Compliance with taxes and other collective obligations is often enforced with resources that come from those who comply, so that non-compliance erodes its own deterrent. We develop an exactly solvable dynamical model of compliance under this fiscal feedback. Individuals choose between paying and evading by imitating those who do better, and the budget against evasion is a share of the revenue, split between enforcement and education. The model yields closed-form expressions for the equilibria, the tipping thresholds and their bifurcations, the budgets needed to maintain compliance and to restore it after a collapse, and the recovery time near the threshold. Fiscal feedback alone does not produce tipping points: hysteresis appears only when an instrument that changes individual incentives, such as fines or education, is funded by the tax base. Stronger sanctions reduce both the maintenance and the rescue budget, but beyond a critical level they make the system bistable, so that the choice of sanction is a trade-off between efficiency and resilience, which we quantify with a resilience indicator and a resilience-constrained design problem. The cheapest allocation of the budget between enforcement and education is also obtained in closed form. A sensitivity analysis identifies the parameters that control prevention and recovery costs, and stochastic simulations of individual agents and a slow budget cycle confirm the analytical predictions. The framework provides quantitative guidelines for allocating scarce intervention resources in tax compliance and in other enforcement problems with similar feedbacks.

papers.title: Computable certificates for data-driven dimension reduction on reaction-diffusion lattices
papers.abstract: Data-driven methods recover low-dimensional coordinates from high-dimensional spatiotemporal data. Whether those coordinates track a genuine invariant object or a finite-resolution artifact is not settled. On reaction-diffusion lattices, the spectral-gap condition of inertial-manifold theory reduces to a critical lattice size $n_*$. Below $n_*$, the two-dimensional diffusion-map reading carries an existence guarantee; above $n_*$ the guarantee lapses, and this lapse does not rule out a slow manifold. The closed form for $n_*$ follows from the reaction Lipschitz constant and the slow-mode growth rate. The certificate is tested on a quadratic and a cubic model system. At the Brusselator boundary the existence sign is checked by interval enclosure, and the spectral margin decays as $n^{-4}$ across the transition. On strongly damped Hopf lattices the slow manifold collapses to the uniform limit cycle; this degeneracy, the trivial graph $\varphi\equiv0$, is reported directly rather than concealed. The boundary gives a PDE-side prior for data-driven reduction: it marks the resolution at which a recovered two-dimensional structure can be trusted.

papers.title: Degree 2 foliations on $\mathbb{P}^2_{\mathbb{C}}$ with only saddle-node and nilpotent singularities
papers.abstract: We classify all foliations of degree $2$ on $\mathbb{P}^2_{\mathbb{C}}$ having only saddle-node or nilpotent singularities up to projective equivalence. To do so, we use the bijection between such foliations and their polar configurations stated by Campillo and Olivares~\cite{CO}. We also show that three families of the found foliations admit no algebraic invariant curve.

papers.title: On the Finite-Time Singularities of Point-Vortex Systems II: Upper Right Quadrant
papers.abstract: We study finite-time singularities of point-vortex systems in the upper right quadrant. For two vortices with arbitrary nonzero circulations and distinct initial positions, we prove global existence and uniqueness by excluding interior collisions, boundary approach, and finite-time escape to infinity. For three vortices with arbitrary nonzero circulations, we rule out finite-time boundary approach in the limit inferior sense, without assuming boundedness or convergence of the trajectories. The argument combines Hamiltonian estimates, monotonicity of signed coordinate moments, and geometric estimates adapted to both walls and the corner. We also establish the existence of finite-time interior collapse for every nonzero circulation triple whose pairwise products sum to zero. The collapse point can be prescribed arbitrarily in the interior, with any sufficiently small positive collapse time. The resulting solutions are asymptotically self-similar, exhibiting square-root contraction and logarithmic rotation. They are constructed using a local strong stable manifold of real dimension two in a similarity system augmented by a complex scale.

papers.title: Genus and Gonality of Small Curves, Dynamical Uniform Boundedness, and Bifurcation
papers.abstract: We prove that a complex one-parameter algebraic family of endomorphisms of $\mathbb{P}^N$ has a non-empty bifurcation set if and only if the genus grows superlinearly in degree along every generic sequence of dynatomic curves. In this case, gonality also tends to infinity. In particular, for non-isotrivial families on $\mathbb{P}^1$, gonality tends to infinity along distinct dynatomic curves, while superlinear genus growth holds for every such sequence exactly when the family is not a flexible Latt\`es family. We also establish analogous results for generic sequences of small curves. As applications, we prove uniform boundedness results for iterated preimages over number fields and geometric uniform boundedness results for preperiodic points over function fields. The proof combines arithmetic equidistribution, woven currents, and bifurcation theory. The bifurcation mechanism is what forces the growth of genus and gonality.

papers.title: Measure-class classification of achievable Cantorvals
papers.abstract: An achievable Cantorval is a Cantorval that is the set of subsums of a convergent series of positive terms. We construct an explicit achievable Cantorval whose boundary has Lebesgue measure at least $2\prod_{j\ge 1}(1-2^{-j})=0.5775\ldots$. This answers a question of G{\l}{\k{a}}b and Prus-Wi{\'s}niowski and gives a counterexample to the conjecture of Nowakowski and Prus-Wi{\'s}niowski that every achievable Cantorval is standard. The example is generated by a hybrid series of Pratsiovytyi, Vynnyshyn and Vynnyshyn. The lower bound comes from an isolated-digit criterion, which produces a Cantor subset of the boundary whose measure is an explicit infinite product; after rescaling, the boundary measure can be made arbitrarily close to $1$. We also prove that the boundary of every achievement set is either Lebesgue null or has positive measure near each of its points. Consequently, up to homeomorphisms that preserve Lebesgue null sets in both directions, there are exactly two achievable Cantorvals, distinguished by whether the boundary is null. For boundaries of positive measure, the homeomorphism can be chosen so that it changes the normalized boundary measure of every Borel set by a factor arbitrarily close to $1$. For general Cantorvals we classify the case of a relatively clopen boundary support and show that further invariants appear beyond this case. Finally, the null-set preserving self-homeomorphisms of a Cantorval always form a meager subgroup of its homeomorphism group. This subgroup is dense exactly when the support of Lebesgue measure on the boundary is empty or the whole boundary; in particular, it is dense for every achievable Cantorval.

papers.title: Correspondence between orbit equivalences and exact symplectomorphisms for Anosov flows
papers.abstract: We show that for a closed hyperbolic $3$-manifold, two Anosov flows are orbital equivalent if and only if the corresponding Anosov Liouville structures are exact symplectomorphic.

papers.title: Sharp $s$-nice recurrence without the van der Corput property
papers.abstract: For every real $s>2$, we construct a set $R_s\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ which is a set of $t$-nice measurable recurrence exactly for $t\ge s$ and is not a van der Corput set. The new ingredient of this construction is the Density Frankl--R\"odl theorem. Furthermore, the probability measure $\sigma_s$ which witnesses failure of the van der Corput property has an atom at zero with mass $(s-2)/(2s-2)$. A Gaussian tail argument proves both sharpness of the recurrence exponent and the fact that this atom is the largest possible for any $s$-nice recurrent set. The result sharpens the recurrence separations of Bourgain and Mountakis, answers a question of Mountakis about the maximal mass of an atom at zero, and answers a question of Forrest about separating the various degrees of nice recurrence. In the appendix we give a self-contained proof of the Density Frankl-R\"odl theorem.

papers.title: KAM theory for contact Hamiltonian systems
papers.abstract: In both finite and infinite dimensions, we establish the first frequency-preserving KAM theorems for full-dimensional Legendrian tori in contact Hamiltonian families with general analytic coupling between the momenta and the contact variable. After adjustment of external parameters, the flow on each torus is analytically conjugate in the original time to the prescribed translation, with estimates uniform as the damping parameter crosses zero. This coupling can generate nonzero mean damping at first order even when the damping parameter vanishes. In finite dimensions, nonzero mean damping yields a time-preserving analytic contact linearization near the torus. In both settings the invariant graphs give global analytic solutions of stationary Hamilton--Jacobi equations whose characteristic flows are conjugate to the prescribed translation. A novel consequence in finite dimensions is that, under global Tonelli assumptions and strict increase in the contact variable, this analytic solution is both the unique forward and the unique backward weak KAM solution, and its associated Legendrian graph is an invariant torus carrying quasi-periodic dynamics.

papers.title: Vector Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals, higher derivatives of Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals and boundedness of solutions of functional-differential equations of retarded type
papers.abstract: In present paper, for functional-differential equations of retarded type, the method of vector Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals and the method of higher derivatives of Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals are developed. On the basis of this methods, sufficient conditions for various types of uniform boundedness of solutions and sufficient conditions for various types of ultimate-uniform boundedness of solutions are obtained.

papers.title: Coordinate Ordering and Non-collinear Central Configurations
papers.abstract: We establish a mass-independent criterion for N-body central configurations based on a special coordinate ordering of the bodies. Moreover, we identify a region in the plane that contains no non-collinear central configurations. This provides a way to exclude non-collinear central configurations that are nearly collinear.

papers.title: The Dynamical Manin-Mumford Conjecture for automorphisms of H\'enon type
papers.abstract: We prove the dynamical Manin--Mumford conjecture for polynomial automorphisms of the complex affine plane of dynamical degree $>1$ proposed by Dujardin and Favre. More precisely, we prove that an irreducible algebraic curve contains infinitely many periodic points of such an automorphism if and only if it is the fixed locus of a polynomial involution conjugating some iterate of the automorphism to its inverse.

papers.title: A transitive $C^{1+\alpha}$ surface diffeomorphism with positive entropy has at most one measure of maximal entropy
papers.abstract: Let $0<\alpha\le 1$. On a closed surface, every topologically transitive $C^{1+\alpha}$ diffeomorphism with positive topological entropy has at most one measure of maximal entropy.

papers.title: Bounds on periods of curves for split rational maps
papers.abstract: Let $A_1$ and $A_2$ be fixed complex rational maps of degree at least two, and let $(A_1,A_2)$ denote the endomorphism of $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$ of the form $(x,y)\mapsto(A_1(x),A_2(y))$. We show that the periods of irreducible $(A_1,A_2)$-periodic curves with dominant coordinate projections are bounded, unless $A_1$ and $A_2$ belong to the exceptional power, Chebyshev, or Latt\`es families. We also extend this result to periodic subvarieties for endomorphisms of $(\mathbb P^1)^m$.

papers.title: Eight limit cycles in a three-dimensional competitive Lotka-Volterra system
papers.abstract: Gyllenberg and Yan conjectured that a three-dimensional competitive Lotka-Volterra system can have at least five limit cycles. We prove the conjecture by constructing a strictly competitive system in which eight distinct limit cycles coexist near a single positive equilibrium. For each $m=5,6,7,8$, we construct a weak focus of order $m$ and identify parameter directions on the Hopf hypersurface that allow us to vary the first $m-1$ focus quantities independently. We choose these quantities so that the drift of a scalar amplitude function alternates in sign on $m$ nested level curves, forcing a limit cycle between each consecutive pair. A perturbation transverse to the Hopf hypersurface creates one additional cycle inside the others. The one-turn displacement map shows that both local counts are sharp. For each $m$, we give a rigorous computer-assisted proof that an explicit rational interaction matrix yields at least $m$ distinct hyperbolic limit cycles. We thank GPT-6 Astra for helping us compare earlier constructions, identify the main obstacle to extending them, and develop the present approach.

papers.title: Nonvanishing of mean indices and stability of symmetric closed characteristics on symmetric star-shaped hypersurfaces in ${\bf R}^4$
papers.abstract: H. Duan, H. Liu, Y. Long and W. Wang \cite{DLLW24} conjectured that if a compact star-shaped hypersurface in ${\bf R}^{2n}$ carries only finitely many geometrically distinct prime closed characteristics, then each of them has nonzero mean index. They proved this conjecture for non-degenerate star-shaped hypersurfaces in ${\bf R}^6$. Motivated by their work, we study the symmetric counterpart of this problem. We prove that if a symmetric compact star-shaped hypersurface $\Sigma$ in ${\bf R}^4$ carries only finitely many geometrically distinct prime symmetric closed characteristics, and every odd iterate of them is non-degenerate in the symmetric sense, then each of them has nonzero symmetric mean index. Based on this result, we further prove that if $\Sigma$ carries exactly two geometrically distinct prime symmetric closed characteristics and all their iterates are non-degenerate, then both of them are irrationally elliptic.

papers.title: High order tangencies, paratangencies, and universal dynamics
papers.abstract: Our research focuses on studying the dynamics in the Newhouse domain $\mathcal N(L)$ -- open regions in the space of $C^r$ diffeomorphisms of a $d$-dimensional manifold $\mathcal M^d$ ($r=1,\ldots,\infty,\omega$ and $d\ge 2$) where homoclinic tangencies to a saddle periodic orbit $L$ are persistent. We prove that diffeomorphisms with infinitely many corank-1 homoclinic tangencies of all orders are dense in such regions. If $L$ is a bi-focus, we reveal novel bifurcations in $\mathcal N(L)$ showing density of diffeomorphisms with infinitely many corank-2 homoclinic tangencies of all orders. These results entail genericity of one- or two-dimensional universal dynamics in $\mathcal N(L)$ (depending on the type of $L$). Moreover, we characterize the geometric complexity of the bifurcation sets corresponding to homoclinic tangencies. We prove that parametric families with paratangencies of arbitrarily high orders are dense in the space of parametric families intersecting $\mathcal N(L)$. If $r\le\infty$ and $L$ is sectionally dissipative, this implies density of families possessing infinitely many coexisting stable periodic orbits for some open set of parameter values.
